In Java, 10,000 requests wait on a blocking call (simulated with a 100 ms Thread.sleep). A thread runs one request and, in a traditional pool, each one holds an operating system thread, which is expensive: with 200 threads, only 200 requests wait at a time and the rest queue up. A virtual thread is managed by the JVM and doesn't hold the OS thread while it waits. But the bottleneck moves: with a pool of 50 connections (a Semaphore), the queue comes back at the connections.

Measured on this machine: OpenJDK 25.0.4.1, Ryzen 7 5700U, 15 runs, a fresh JVM each run. Medians: pool of 200 threads 5,088.6 ms; virtual threads 179.4 ms; virtual threads with 50 connections 20,139 ms. The wait is simulated, not a real network or database.

Mechanism sources: JEP 444 (Virtual Threads) and the JDK 25 Executors documentation.

The voice is mine, cloned with AI. The animations were made for this video.
